Top 10 Personalised Wedding Guest Book Trends for UK Couples in 2025

Planning a wedding in the UK for 2025 involves balancing timeless tradition with modern innovation. One of the most cherished keepsakes from any big day is the guest book—a collection of well-wishes from family and friends. However, the days of a simple blank book with lined paper are quickly being replaced by interactive, sensory, and highly personalised alternatives.

The quick answer: For 2025, the biggest trend is multimedia integration. UK couples are moving away from handwritten notes alone and embracing technologies like SayPlay Voice Message Stickers, which allow guests to leave audio or video messages directly inside a physical book using simple QR technology.

In this comprehensive guide, we explore the top 10 personalised wedding guest book trends that will dominate the UK wedding scene in 2025.

1. SayPlay Voice Message Stickers: The Interactive Revolution

Leading the pack for 2025 is the integration of digital media into physical books. SayPlay Voice Message Stickers have transformed the traditional guest book into a living, breathing archive of the wedding day. Instead of just reading a message, you can hear the laughter of your bridesmaids or see a quick 30-second video of your grandparents offering advice.

These stickers are small, elegant QR codes that guests scan with their smartphones—no app required. They record a message, and it is instantly linked to that sticker. For UK couples looking for a mix of modern tech and classic scrapbooking, this is the gold standard.

  • Visuals: Small, discreet stickers that fit perfectly next to photos or handwritten notes.
  • Benefit: It captures the actual tone and emotion of the day that text simply cannot replicate.

2. The Vintage Audio Guest Book (Retro Telephones)

The "audio guest book" trend continues to grow in 2025. This involves using a converted vintage 1970s or 80s telephone. Guests pick up the receiver, hear a recorded greeting from the couple, and leave their message after the beep. While visually stunning as a prop on a dedicated table, many couples are now combining this with physical books by printing the transcripts or using audio stickers to save the recordings permanently in an album.

3. Instant Photo & Scrapbook Stations

The nostalgia of Polaroid and Instax cameras remains a staple for UK weddings. In 2025, the trend evolves into "The Curated Scrapbook." Couples provide metallic pens, decorative washi tape, and pre-designed prompts. Guests take a photo, stick it in, and write a message. When combined with SayPlay stickers, this creates a triple-threat memory: a photo, a written note, and a voice message all on one page.

4. Custom Illustration Books

Bespoke stationery is huge for 2025. Many UK couples are commissioning artists to create custom illustrations of their venue, their pets, or themselves to feature on the cover and throughout the pages of the guest book. These books act more like coffee table art pieces than simple logs of attendees.

5. Wooden Puzzle Piece Guest Books

For a tactile and symbolic option, "The Missing Piece" guest book is trending. Guests sign individual wooden puzzle pieces that, when completed, form a large heart or an image of the couple. It’s a popular choice for rustic barn weddings in the Cotswolds or rural Yorkshire, doubling as a piece of wall art for the couple's home after the event.

6. Vinyl Record Guest Books

Music-loving couples are opting for "The Soundtrack of Our Lives." They provide vintage vinyl records or custom-pressed discs with their wedding date on the label. Guests sign the vinyl using silver or gold permanent markers. It’s sleek, visual, and fits perfectly into the "cool Britannia" aesthetic often seen in London industrial venue weddings.

7. Message in a Bottle (Anniversary Capsules)

Instead of one book, couples provide several glass bottles labelled "1st Anniversary," "5th Anniversary," and "10th Anniversary." Guests write messages and drop them into the bottle of their choice. This trend focuses on the longevity of the marriage, providing a "slow-burn" reward for the couple as they reach milestones over the next decade.
